summary.text: At \(N=249580077006\), a finite recurrence calculation for the coefficients and fast-doubling Fibonacci computations modulo \(p=195318521017\) show that the claimed Fibonacci formula would make both \(a_N\) and \(a_{N+1}\) divisible by \(p\). Their gcd would therefore exceed \(1\), but for positive consecutive terms the defining update \(g+(a_N+a_{N+1})/g\) cannot equal \(1+a_N+a_{N+1}\) when \(g>1\), contradicting the claimed formula at \(N+2\).

full_proof.text:
Let \((a_n)\) be the sequence defined by
\[
a_1=a_2=1,\qquad
 a_n=g_n+\frac{a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}}{g_n}\quad(n\geq 3),
\]
where \(g_n=\gcd(a_{n-1},a_{n-2})\). We disprove the assertion that all three proposed formulas hold for every \(n\geq3775\). In fact, only the first and third proposed formulas will be needed.

Put
\[
 p=195318521017,
 \qquad N=249580077006.
\]
Certainly \(N,N+1,N+2\geq3775\).

We first record the finite computations on which the counterexample rests. Starting with the pair \((1,1)\), repeatedly replace a consecutive pair \((x,y)\) by
\[
 \left(y,\ \gcd(x,y)+\frac{x+y}{\gcd(x,y)}\right).
\]
After 3770 and 3772 such updates, respectively, one obtains
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{3772}={}&,\\[2mm]
a_{3774}={}&.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is simply a finite evaluation of the defining recurrence; every division is exact because the gcd divides both entries and hence their sum. Reducing these two integers modulo \(p\) gives
\[
 a_{3774}+1\equiv 99768150822\pmod p,
 \qquad
 a_{3772}+1\equiv 21827756563\pmod p.
\]
For brevity set
\[
 \alpha=a_{3774}+1,\qquad \beta=a_{3772}+1.
\]
Thus
\[
 \alpha\equiv99768150822\pmod p,
 \qquad \beta\equiv21827756563\pmod p. \tag{1}
\]

We also need four Fibonacci residues. They are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
 m&F_m\pmod p\\ \hline
 N-3774=249580073232&117378126758\\
 N-3772=249580073234&139205883321\\
 N+1-3774=249580073233&21827756563\\
 N+1-3772=249580073235&161033639884.
\end{array} \tag{2}
\]
Here is a reproducible description of this modular computation. Starting from \((F_0,F_1)=(0,1)\), read the binary expansion of the desired index from left to right. If the pair currently held is \((F_k,F_{k+1})\), calculate modulo \(p\)
\[
 F_{2k}=F_k(2F_{k+1}-F_k),
 \qquad
 F_{2k+1}=F_k^2+F_{k+1}^2,
 \qquad
 F_{2k+2}=F_{2k}+F_{2k+1}.
\]
For a binary digit 0 replace the pair by \((F_{2k},F_{2k+1})\), and for a binary digit 1 replace it by \((F_{2k+1},F_{2k+2})\). The four binary inputs are
\[
\begin{aligned}
249580073232&=(11101000011100001000011011000100010000)_2,\\
249580073234&=(11101000011100001000011011000100010010)_2,\\
249580073233&=(11101000011100001000011011000100010001)_2,\\
249580073235&=(11101000011100001000011011000100010011)_2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Applying the displayed doubling rules gives exactly the four residues in (2). These identities follow directly from the standard Fibonacci addition formulas, so this computes the same Fibonacci numbers as the recurrence \(F_0=0,F_1=1,F_{m+2}=F_{m+1}+F_m\).

Combining (1) and (2), the modular products at \(N\) are
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \alpha F_{N-3772}
 &\equiv99768150822\cdot139205883321
 \equiv173297039858\pmod p,\\
 \beta F_{N-3774}
 &\equiv21827756563\cdot117378126758
 \equiv173297039857\pmod p.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \alpha F_{N-3772}-\beta F_{N-3774}\equiv1\pmod p. \tag{3}
\]
Likewise, at \(N+1\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \alpha F_{N+1-3772}
 &\equiv99768150822\cdot161033639884
 \equiv42879902104\pmod p,\\
 \beta F_{N+1-3774}
 &\equiv21827756563\cdot21827756563
 \equiv42879902103\pmod p,
\end{aligned}
\]
and hence
\[
 \alpha F_{N+1-3772}-\beta F_{N+1-3774}\equiv1\pmod p. \tag{4}
\]

Now suppose, for contradiction, that the conjecture is true for every index at least 3775. Its first formula at \(N\) and \(N+1\) says
\[
 a_N=1+a_{N-1}+a_{N-2},
 \qquad
 a_{N+1}=1+a_N+a_{N-1}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 a_N\geq1,\qquad a_{N+1}\geq1. \tag{5}
\]

The third conjectured formula at \(N\) is
\[
 a_N=\alpha F_{N-3772}-\beta F_{N-3774}-1. \tag{6}
\]
If the subtractions in this formula are interpreted as ordinary integer subtraction, rearranging immediately gives
\[
 a_N+\beta F_{N-3774}+1=\alpha F_{N-3772}. \tag{7}
\]
The same conclusion also follows if, as in a sequence of natural numbers, the minus signs are interpreted as truncated natural-number subtraction: because the left side of (6) is positive by (5), neither subtraction can have truncated the expression to zero. Thus (7) is valid under either convention. Reducing (7) modulo \(p\) and using (3) yields
\[
 a_N\equiv0\pmod p;
\]
that is,
\[
 p\mid a_N. \tag{8}
\]

The identical argument at \(N+1\) uses
\[
 a_{N+1}=\alpha F_{N+1-3772}-\beta F_{N+1-3774}-1
\]
and positivity from (5), giving
\[
 a_{N+1}+\beta F_{N+1-3774}+1
 =\alpha F_{N+1-3772}.
\]
Together with (4), this implies
\[
 p\mid a_{N+1}. \tag{9}
\]

Let
\[
 g=\gcd(a_{N+1},a_N),\qquad x=a_{N+1}+a_N.
\]
By (8) and (9), \(p\mid g\). The two terms are positive by (5), so \(g>0\), and therefore
\[
 g\geq p>1. \tag{10}
\]
Also, \(g\mid x\).

The actual defining recurrence at index \(N+2\) gives
\[
 a_{N+2}=g+\frac{x}{g}. \tag{11}
\]
On the other hand, the first conjectured formula, now at \(N+2\), gives
\[
 a_{N+2}=1+a_{N+1}+a_N=1+x. \tag{12}
\]
Equating (11) and (12), and writing \(x=gt\) with \(t=x/g\), gives
\[
 g+t=1+gt.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
 (g-1)(t-1)=0. \tag{13}
\]
Since \(g>1\), equation (13) forces \(t=1\), hence \(x=g\).

That is impossible. Since \(g\) divides each of the positive integers \(a_N\) and \(a_{N+1}\), each is at least \(g\). Therefore
\[
 x=a_N+a_{N+1}\geq2g>g,
\]
contradicting \(x=g\).

Thus the conjectured formulas cannot hold for every \(n\geq3775\). More specifically, the simultaneous validity of the third formula at \(N\) and \(N+1\), together with the first formula at \(N\), \(N+1\), and \(N+2\), already produces a contradiction. Hence the stated universal conjecture for A355898 is false.
